1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Cases for the claim that orca.nix runs the Orca GUI unsandboxed: the

    11	# from the host, only from a process the app spawns, so these cases probe from
    12	# one.

    16	# through `systemd-run --user`, whose units the user manager starts outside it.

    19	# resources/node-runtime, whose node is copied into orcad slots and checked
    20	# against a sha256 pin in app.asar (a patched node fails the check, and Orca
    21	# falls back to downloading stock node), and resources/orcad-template, whose
    22	# per-target builds (arm64, musl) are shipped to remote hosts.
    23	#

    25	# only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 -- ask before setting it on someone's session.
    26	# It starts a second instance with its own --user-data-dir and a throwaway
    27	# HOME, so it never touches the running Orca's profile, its
    28	# ~/.orca/agent-hooks or ~/.claude/settings.json.

    35	set -o pipefail

    41	FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)

    43	if [ -e /etc/hostname ]; then
    44	  host() { "$@"; }

    72	  fail "no sandbox" "bubblewrap is in the closure of $ORCA"

    83	# rejects ("bad option", exit 9). orca's CLI probes the GUI this way.

    86	  || fail "node mode" "printed '$got', want 1"
    87	
    88	# 3. What a spawned process sees is the host: hostname, zone, fonts.
    89	node_run() { # node_run <shell command>: run it from a child of the GUI in node mode
    90	  host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \
    91	    'process.stdout.write(require("child_process").execFileSync("/bin/sh", ["-c", process.argv[1]]))' \
    92	    "$1" 2>&1

    98	done

   104	  || fail "DejaVu" "app's fontconfig has '${got:-nothing}'"

   106	  pat=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
   107	  got=$(node_run "fc-match -f '%{family[0]}' '$pat'")
   108	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$pat -> $want for the app" \
   109	    || fail "$pat" "resolves to '${got:-nothing}', want '$want'"
   110	done
   111	
   112	# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty, loaded by this Electron, opens a pty.
   113	got=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
   114	  const p = require(process.argv[1]).spawn("/bin/sh", ["-c", "echo pty-ok"], {});
   115	  let o = ""; p.onData(d => o += d); p.onExit(e => console.log(o.trim(), e.exitCode));' \
   116	  "$APP/resources/node_modules/node-pty" 2>&1)
   117	[ "$got" = "pty-ok 0" ] && pass "node-pty opens a pty" || fail "node-pty" "got '$got'"
   118	
   119	# 4. Every native ELF of this arch resolves all its libraries on the host.
   120	mapfile -t elfs < <(find "$APP" -type f \( -name '*.so*' -o -name '*.node' -o -perm -u+x \) \
   121	  -not -path '*/orcad-template/*' -print0 \
   122	  | host xargs -0 file | grep -E 'ELF 64-bit LSB .*(executable|shared object), x86-64' | cut -d: -f1)

   124	  fail "ELFs" "only ${#elfs[@]} found under $APP"
   125	else

   128	    || fail "ldd" "$(printf '\n%s' "$missing")"
   129	fi
   130	
   131	# 5. The pinned trees are the AppImage's, byte for byte -- not patched, not
   132	# stripped, no shebang rewritten. The derivation's src is the extracted
   133	# AppImage, so it is on this machine whenever the build is.
   134	src=$(nix derivation show "$(nix-store -qd "$APP/../..")" 2>/dev/null \
   135	  | grep -oE '"src": *"/nix/store/[^"]*-extracted"' | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^"]*')
   136	if [ -z "$src" ]; then
   137	  fail "pinned trees" "cannot find the derivation's src for $APP"
   138	else
   139	  for d in resources/node-runtime resources/orcad-template; do
   140	    if out=$(diff -r "$src/$d" "$APP/$d" 2>&1); then
   141	      pass "$d is the AppImage's, unchanged"
   142	    else
   143	      fail "$d" "differs from $src: $(echo "$out" | head -3)"
   144	    fi
   145	  done
   146	fi

   149	pin=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$APP/resources/orcad-template/targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node" 2>/dev/null)

   152	  || fail "node pin" "sha256 '$got', pin '${pin:-missing}'"
   153	
   154	# 6. A real second instance renders, sandboxes its renderers, and stops on
   155	# SIGTERM. Its own --user-data-dir and HOME keep it off the live Orca's state.
   156	if [ "${ORCA_TEST_GUI:-}" != 1 ]; then
   157	  echo "skip GUI launch: it opens a visible window; set ORCA_TEST_GUI=1"
   158	elif [ -z "$(host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY)" ]; then

   167	  for _ in $(seq 40); do

   171	      && host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids," && break
   172	  done
   173	  if host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids,"; then
   174	    pass "a window maps (pid $pids)"
   175	  else

   196	  fi

    63	exe=$(sed -n 's/^Exec=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "$ORCA"/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop | head -1)
    64	GUI="$ORCA/bin/$exe"
    65	[ -n "$exe" ] && [ -x "$GUI" ] || { echo "no GUI bin from $ORCA's desktop Exec ('$exe')" >&2; exit 1; }
    66	echo "testing $GUI"
    67	
    68	T=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.cache/orca-gui-test.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
    69	
    70	# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.
    71	if nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | grep -q -- '-bubblewrap-'; then
    72	  fail "no sandbox" "bubblewrap is in the closure of $ORCA"
    73	else
    74	  pass "no bubblewrap in the closure"
    75	fi
    76	
    77	# The unwrapped tree: where resources/ lives.

    79	  [ -f "$p/lib/orca/resources/app.asar" ] && echo "$p/lib/orca"; done | head -1)

    82	# 2. Node mode: the wrapper must not inject --ozone-platform, which node
    83	# rejects ("bad option", exit 9). orca's CLI probes the GUI this way.

    85	[ "$got" = 1 ] && pass "ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 runs node" \
    86	  || fail "node mode" "printed '$got', want 1"
    87	
    88	# 3. What a spawned process sees is the host: hostname, zone, fonts.
    89	node_run() { # node_run <shell command>: run it from a child of the GUI in node mode
    90	  host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \
    91	    'process.stdout.write(require("child_process").execFileSync("/bin/sh", ["-c", process.argv[1]]))' \
    92	    "$1" 2>&1

    95	  want=$(host /bin/sh -c "$c"); got=$(node_run "$c")
    96	  [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "child sees host's '$c' ($want)" \
    97	    || fail "$c" "child got '$got', host has '$want'"
    98	done
    99	# Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono", one
   100	# family with no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another

   102	got=$(node_run "fc-list -f '%{family[0]}\n' 'DejaVu Sans Mono' | sort -u | head -1")

   104	  || fail "DejaVu" "app's fontconfig has '${got:-nothing}'"

   106	  pat=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
   107	  got=$(node_run "fc-match -f '%{family[0]}' '$pat'")
   108	  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$pat -> $want for the app" \
   109	    || fail "$pat" "resolves to '${got:-nothing}', want '$want'"
   110	done
   111	
   112	# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty, loaded by this Electron, opens a pty.
   113	got=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
   114	  const p = require(process.argv[1]).spawn("/bin/sh", ["-c", "echo pty-ok"], {});
   115	  let o = ""; p.onData(d => o += d); p.onExit(e => console.log(o.trim(), e.exitCode));' \

   119	# 4. Every native ELF of this arch resolves all its libraries on the host.
   120	mapfile -t elfs < <(find "$APP" -type f \( -name '*.so*' -o -name '*.node' -o -perm -u+x \) \
   121	  -not -path '*/orcad-template/*' -print0 \
   122	  | host xargs -0 file | grep -E 'ELF 64-bit LSB .*(executable|shared object), x86-64' | cut -d: -f1)
   123	if [ "${#elfs[@]}" -lt 10 ]; then
   124	  fail "ELFs" "only ${#elfs[@]} found under $APP"
   125	else
   126	  missing=$(host /bin/sh -c 'for f; do ldd "$f" 2>&1 | grep "not found" | sed "s|^|$f: |"; done' sh "${elfs[@]}")

   128	    || fail "ldd" "$(printf '\n%s' "$missing")"
   129	fi

   132	# stripped, no shebang rewritten. The derivation's src is the extracted
   133	# AppImage, so it is on this machine whenever the build is.
   134	src=$(nix derivation show "$(nix-store -qd "$APP/../..")" 2>/dev/null \
   135	  | grep -oE '"src": *"/nix/store/[^"]*-extracted"' | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^"]*')
   136	if [ -z "$src" ]; then
   137	  fail "pinned trees" "cannot find the derivation's src for $APP"
   138	else
   139	  for d in resources/node-runtime resources/orcad-template; do
   140	    if out=$(diff -r "$src/$d" "$APP/$d" 2>&1); then
   141	      pass "$d is the AppImage's, unchanged"
   142	    else
   143	      fail "$d" "differs from $src: $(echo "$out" | head -3)"
   144	    fi
   145	  done
   146	fi
   147	node="$APP/resources/node-runtime/bin/node"
   148	# The slot's runtime reference: what orcad checks the copied node against.
   149	pin=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$APP/resources/orcad-template/targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node" 2>/dev/null)
   150	got=$(sha256sum "$node" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)
   151	[ -n "$pin" ] && [ "$got" = "$pin" ] && pass "bundled node matches orcad's runtime pin" \
   152	  || fail "node pin" "sha256 '$got', pin '${pin:-missing}'"
   153	
   154	# 6. A real second instance renders, sandboxes its renderers, and stops on
   155	# SIGTERM. Its own --user-data-dir and HOME keep it off the live Orca's state.
   156	if [ "${ORCA_TEST_GUI:-}" != 1 ]; then
   157	  echo "skip GUI launch: it opens a visible window; set ORCA_TEST_GUI=1"
   158	elif [ -z "$(host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY)" ]; then
   159	  echo "skip GUI launch: no Wayland session"
   160	else
   161	  unit="orca-gui-test-$$"
   162	  mkdir -p "$T/home"
   163	  since=$(date +%s)
   164	  "${sr:+$sr/bin/}systemd-run" --user --quiet --unit="$unit" --property=KillSignal=SIGTERM \
   165	    --setenv=HOME="$T/home" "$GUI" --user-data-dir="$T/profile"
   166	  pids=""
   167	  for _ in $(seq 40); do
   168	    sleep 1
   169	    pids=$(host systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
   170	    [ -n "$pids" ] && [ "$pids" != 0 ] \
   171	      && host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids," && break
   172	  done
   173	  if host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids,"; then
   174	    pass "a window maps (pid $pids)"
   175	  else
   176	    fail "window" "no Hyprland client for pid '$pids' after 40s"
   177	    host journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager -n 20
   178	  fi
   179	  # Renderers in their own user namespace = Chromium's namespace sandbox,
   180	  # with chrome-sandbox left unprivileged.
   181	  ns=$(host /bin/sh -c '
   182	    main=$(readlink /proc/'"$pids"'/ns/user)
   183	    for p in $(systemctl --user show -p ControlGroup --value '"$unit"' | xargs -I{} cat /sys/fs/cgroup{}/cgroup.procs); do
   184	      tr "\0" " " < /proc/$p/cmdline | grep -q -- "--type=renderer" || continue
   185	      [ "$(readlink /proc/$p/ns/user)" != "$main" ] && echo sandboxed || echo unsandboxed
   186	    done' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
   187	  [ "$ns" = "sandboxed " ] && pass "renderers run in their own user namespace" \
   188	    || fail "chromium sandbox" "renderers: '${ns:-none}'"
   189	  # A transient unit that stopped cleanly is unloaded (show prints nothing);
   190	  # one whose main process exited non-zero stays loaded as failed, with why.
   191	  if host systemctl --user stop "$unit"; then
   192	    res=$(host systemctl --user show -p Result --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
   193	    res=${res:-success}
   194	  else
   195	    res="stop failed"
   196	  fi
   197	  host systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null
   198	  [ "$res" = success ] && pass "stops cleanly on SIGTERM" \
   199	    || fail "SIGTERM" "unit result '$res'"
   200	  cores=$(host coredumpctl list --no-legend --since="@$since" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "$ORCA|orca-ide" || true)
   201	  [ -z "$cores" ] && pass "no coredumps" || fail "coredumps" "$cores"
   202	fi
   203	
   204	printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
   205	[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

+# never touches a running Orca's profile, ~/.orca/agent-hooks or
+# ~/.claude/settings.json. ORCA_TEST_SHOT=<file.png> keeps its screenshot.
 #
 #   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh               build this host's orca and test it
-#   ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh   ... and launch it once

 #                                               $(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))
 set -u

   || fail "node pin" "sha256 '$got', pin '${pin:-missing}'"

-# SIGTERM. Its own --user-data-dir and HOME keep it off the live Orca's state.

-  echo "skip GUI launch: it opens a visible window; set ORCA_TEST_GUI=1"
-elif [ -z "$(host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY)" ]; then
-  echo "skip GUI launch: no Wayland session"
+# 6. A real instance renders, sandboxes its renderers, and exits 0 on
+# SIGTERM -- in a headless sway of its own, so it needs no desktop and never
+# appears on one.
+tools=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$FLAKE" nixpkgs#sway nixpkgs#grim) \
+  || { echo "could not build sway/grim" >&2; exit 1; }
+sway=$(echo "$tools" | grep -- '-sway-'); grim=$(echo "$tools" | grep -- '-grim-')
+run="$T/run"; mkdir -p -m700 "$run"; mkdir -p "$T/home"
+cat > "$T/sway.conf" <<EOF
+output HEADLESS-1 resolution 1280x800
+exec /bin/sh -c '"$GUI" --user-data-dir="$T/profile"; echo \$? > "$T/orca.exit"'
+EOF
+in_session() { host env -u DISPLAY XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$run" WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 "$@"; }
+unit="orca-gui-test-$$"
+since=$(date +%s)
+"${sr:+$sr/bin/}systemd-run" --user --quiet --unit="$unit" --setenv=HOME="$T/home" \
+  --setenv=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$run" --setenv=WLR_BACKENDS=headless --setenv=WLR_RENDERER=pixman \
+  --setenv=WLR_LIBINPUT_NO_DEVICES=1 --setenv=WAYLAND_DISPLAY= --setenv=DISPLAY= \
+  "$sway/bin/sway" -c "$T/sway.conf"
+pid=""
+for _ in $(seq 60); do
+  sleep 1
+  sock=$(ls "$run"/sway-ipc.*.sock 2>/dev/null | head -1)
+  [ -n "$sock" ] || continue
+  in_session "$sway/bin/swaymsg" -s "$sock" -t get_tree > "$T/tree.json" 2>/dev/null || continue
+  pid=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
+    const walk = n => n.app_id === "orca" ? n.pid : [...n.nodes, ...n.floating_nodes].map(walk).find(Boolean);
+    console.log(walk(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1]))) || "");' "$T/tree.json")
+  [ -n "$pid" ] && break
+done
+if [ -z "$pid" ]; then
+  fail "window" "no orca window in the headless session after 60s"
+  host journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager -n 20
 else
-  unit="orca-gui-test-$$"
-  mkdir -p "$T/home"
-  since=$(date +%s)
-  "${sr:+$sr/bin/}systemd-run" --user --quiet --unit="$unit" --property=KillSignal=SIGTERM \
-    --setenv=HOME="$T/home" "$GUI" --user-data-dir="$T/profile"
-  pids=""
-  for _ in $(seq 40); do
-    sleep 1
-    pids=$(host systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
-    [ -n "$pids" ] && [ "$pids" != 0 ] \
-      && host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids," && break
-  done
-  if host hyprctl clients -j 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\"pid\": $pids,"; then
-    pass "a window maps (pid $pids)"
-  else
-    fail "window" "no Hyprland client for pid '$pids' after 40s"
-    host journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager -n 20
-  fi
+  pass "a window maps (pid $pid)"

+  # a handful of colours, a rendered UI with antialiased text has hundreds.
+  sleep 10
+  in_session "$grim/bin/grim" -t ppm "$T/shot.ppm"
+  colours=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
+    const b = require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1]);
+    let i = 0, f = 0; const tok = () => { while (/\s/.test(String.fromCharCode(b[i]))) i++;
+      const s = i; while (!/\s/.test(String.fromCharCode(b[i]))) i++; return b.slice(s, i).toString(); };
+    tok(); tok(); tok(); tok(); i++;
+    const seen = new Set(); for (; i + 2 < b.length; i += 3) seen.add((b[i] << 16) | (b[i+1] << 8) | b[i+2]);
+    console.log(seen.size);' "$T/shot.ppm" 2>&1)
+  [ "${colours:-0}" -gt 100 ] 2>/dev/null && pass "it renders a UI ($colours colours on screen)" \
+    || fail "render" "screen has '$colours' colours; blank or broken"
+  if [ -n "${ORCA_TEST_SHOT:-}" ]; then in_session "$grim/bin/grim" "$ORCA_TEST_SHOT"; fi
   # Renderers in their own user namespace = Chromium's namespace sandbox,
   # with chrome-sandbox left unprivileged.
   ns=$(host /bin/sh -c '
-    main=$(readlink /proc/'"$pids"'/ns/user)
-    for p in $(systemctl --user show -p ControlGroup --value '"$unit"' | xargs -I{} cat /sys/fs/cgroup{}/cgroup.procs); do
-      tr "\0" " " < /proc/$p/cmdline | grep -q -- "--type=renderer" || continue
+    main=$(readlink /proc/'"$pid"'/ns/user)
+    for p in $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup$(systemctl --user show -p ControlGroup --value '"$unit"')/cgroup.procs); do
+      tr "\0" " " < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | grep -q -- "--type=renderer" || continue
       [ "$(readlink /proc/$p/ns/user)" != "$main" ] && echo sandboxed || echo unsandboxed
     done' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
   [ "$ns" = "sandboxed " ] && pass "renderers run in their own user namespace" \
     || fail "chromium sandbox" "renderers: '${ns:-none}'"
-  # A transient unit that stopped cleanly is unloaded (show prints nothing);
-  # one whose main process exited non-zero stays loaded as failed, with why.
-  if host systemctl --user stop "$unit"; then
-    res=$(host systemctl --user show -p Result --value "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
-    res=${res:-success}
-  else
-    res="stop failed"
-  fi
-  host systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null
-  [ "$res" = success ] && pass "stops cleanly on SIGTERM" \
-    || fail "SIGTERM" "unit result '$res'"
-  cores=$(host coredumpctl list --no-legend --since="@$since" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "$ORCA|orca-ide" || true)
-  [ -z "$cores" ] && pass "no coredumps" || fail "coredumps" "$cores"
+  # SIGTERM to the window's own pid, which this case started: the wrappers
+  # all exec, so it is Electron itself, with nothing in between.
+  host kill -TERM "$pid"
+  for _ in $(seq 20); do [ -s "$T/orca.exit" ] && break; sleep 1; done
+  code=$(cat "$T/orca.exit" 2>/dev/null)
+  [ "$code" = 0 ] && pass "exits 0 on SIGTERM" || fail "SIGTERM" "exit status '${code:-none after 20s}'"
 fi
+host systemctl --user stop "$unit" 2>/dev/null
+host systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null
+cores=$(host coredumpctl list --no-legend --since="@$since" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "$ORCA|orca-ide" || true)
+[ -z "$cores" ] && pass "no coredumps" || fail "coredumps" "$cores"
 
 printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
 [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]
